question: As on 31st May 2020, how many languages enjoy the status of classical language in India?
solution:
The correct answer is__** 6.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A** language** that has a **substantial and lengthy corpus** of** written literature**, as well as its **own autonomous literary tradition**, is said to be** classical.**
 
• Classical languages have **advantages** such as the** establishment of study centres** and the **provision of international awards for its scholars.**
 
• **Six languages** currently hold the designation of "Classical":
 
 
• Tamil (announced in 2004),
 
• Sanskrit (2005),
 
• Kannada (2008),
 
• Telugu (2008),
 
• Malayalam (2013), and
 
• Odia (2014).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **criteria for designating** a language as **"Classical"** are as follows:

 
 
• High antiquity of its **early texts/recorded history **over a period of **1500–2000 years;**
 
• A **body of ancient literature/texts, **which is regarded as a **priceless legacy** by** generations of speakers;**
 
• The **literary tradition** be **original and not borrowed** from another speech community;
 
• The classical language and literature **being distinct from modern,** there may also be a** discontinuity **between the classical language and its **later forms or its offshoots."**
